items.title: Viewer panes
items.text: Panes (or whole windows) can now render content instead of a terminal: markdown files with GitHub-style rendering (fully offline — tables, task lists, syntax-highlighted code, images), plain text/code files with syntax highlighting, and websites. Open them with `--view` on `+new-window` or `+split`, from the command palette, or via File → Open / dragging a `.md` file onto the dock. Viewers live in the normal split tree — they resize, focus, zoom, split, and close like any pane, follow light/dark appearance, and restore with session persistence. File viewers live-reload on save (preserving scroll position), and relative markdown links open in a new viewer split.

items.title: Window titles
items.text: Press Cmd+Shift+R to set a window-level title that pins the titlebar until cleared, winning over tab and pane titles and surviving shell title updates. Also scriptable via `ghoztty +rename --title` (empty title clears the pin), with separate Change Tab Title and Change Pane Title commands in the menu and palette.

items.title: Banner tables & polish
items.text: Pane banners now render markdown pipe tables as aligned grids with bold headers, plus alignment markers. Banners got symmetric padding, a shaded background, and a collapse toggle.

items.title: Sign-in without secrets
items.text: Google sign-in now uses relay-brokered OAuth: the app holds only a short-lived session token and no client secret ships in the binary. Sign-in, renewal, and sign-out all flow through the relay.

items.title: Easier split dragging
items.text: Split dividers now have a real ~9pt grab target, so resizing panes no longer requires pixel-perfect aim. Web viewer panes get an auto-hiding browser chrome that stays out of the way.

items.title: Session persistence fixes
items.text: Closing a pane now reliably ends its persistent session (no orphaned processes), re-attached terminals keep correct PTY geometry, and quitting the app no longer warns about terminating sessions that actually survive the quit. Every pane also gets a stable id (`$GHOZTTY_PANE_ID`) that survives restarts, restores, and reconnects — the reliable way for scripts to target their own pane.
Protocol and connection-handling improvements to the remote agent; a new agent build ships alongside this release and installed agents pick it up automatically on their next idle self-update check.
